matches.rationale: No finding addresses fabricated dataset variants (antmaze-large-diverse, maze2d-large) or invented benchmark splits. The findings cover speedup claims, undefined algorithms, figure-text inconsistencies, loss equation discrepancies, and ill-formed equations—none of which relate to the dataset fabrication issue.

No finding identifies the asymmetric hyperparameter tuning budget across algorithms or the unequal constraints in the evaluation protocol. The findings address entirely different concerns such as numerical inconsistencies in speedup claims and equation definitions.

Finding 4 identifies an inconsistency between Section 4.2 and Appendix I.2 in the unified actor loss definition regarding β_div and β_dyn terms. This captures the same underlying scientific issue as GT 3, which states the unified actor loss omits critic diversity loss and model-based regularization terms and contains partial/conflicting definitions that reduce logical completeness. Both pinpoint the incomplete and inconsistent formulation of the unified actor objective across paper sections.

GT 4 concerns missing hardware specifications, parallelization details, and compilation/caching information that undermine reproducibility of speedup claims. Finding 1 identifies a numerical discrepancy in speedup values between abstract and body. While both involve speedup claims, they address different scientific issues: one is about omitted methodological details, the other about factually inconsistent numbers.

GT 5 concerns selective reporting (omitted error bars, ignoring datasets where performance is similar or worse) to inflate perception of superiority. Finding 3 identifies a specific text-figure contradiction about TD3-AWR vs ReBRAC on pen-human. These are different scientific issues: reporting integrity versus factual accuracy of a single data point.

No finding addresses the Conclusion section's exaggerated claims about Unifloral combining improvements and achieving superior performance over a wide range of tasks. None of the six findings mention the conclusion or these specific overclaims.

No finding mentions the absence of ethical considerations or safety risks in the Introduction. The findings are exclusively focused on technical issues such as numerical claims, undefined algorithms, equation errors, and definitional inconsistencies.

No finding addresses the Related Work section, fabricated or misrepresented citations [25, 26, 27], or the selective depiction of prior unification work. Finding 2 mentions an undefined algorithm (LB-SAC) but this is unrelated to citation fabrication.

GT 9 identifies inflated promotional rhetoric in the Abstract (e.g., 'significantly enhancing', 'substantial speed-ups'). Finding 1 identifies a specific factual error in speedup numbers in the Abstract. While both target the Abstract and relate to speedup claims, the scientific issues differ: rhetorical exaggeration versus demonstrably false quantitative claims.

No finding addresses the contradictory inclusion/exclusion of CQL between Section 4.2 (omitted for complexity) and Appendix A.1 (included in reimplementations). None of the six findings mention CQL or this cross-section inconsistency.

GT 11 concerns pseudocode inconsistencies in Appendix blocks #75-77 regarding EDAC vs SAC-N/CQL actor loss aggregation (mean vs min) and diversity regularization. Findings 5 and 6 address ill-formed equations in Appendix I.1 (missing case conditions and undefined variables), which are different appendix locations and fundamentally different errors.

No finding mentions tight y-axis scaling, selective axis choices, or graphical distortion in Figures 3, 6, and 7. Finding 3 addresses a figure-text value contradiction but not axis manipulation or visual exaggeration of effect sizes.
No finding addresses the Acknowledgements section or the omission of explicit conflict of interest disclosures. All findings are concerned with technical content in the main body or appendices.

No finding addresses the contradiction between the four-variant taxonomy in Sections 1 and 3 and the exclusive focus on pre-deployment tuning (Setting 2a) in Section 3.2. None of the six findings discuss the offline RL setting taxonomy or its internal coherence.

No finding addresses the distractor policy phenomenon, the interpretation of performance curve dips, or the claim that fluctuations are over-interpreted as evaluation flaws. The findings cover unrelated issues such as speedup claims, undefined algorithms, and equation errors.
